S29.17.note: No insert-chart button, menu or dialog found. Charts are built by the assistant only when asked for an .xlsx workbook: managed-workbook-builder and managed-office-file-service take a per-sheet chart (bar, line, pie) from the sheet's own cells. Searched 'Insert chart', 'Add chart', 'Chart type' and 'chart' in the chat and artifact files.

S29.18.needs: a request to the assistant for a slide deck with a chart
S29.18.note: The selector exists only in the slide-deck chart editor, not for charts in a spreadsheet or the chart artifact. Options are Bar, Line and Pie.
steps: Ask the assistant for a slide deck that contains a chart, and wait for the deck to appear in the artifact panel.
Click the button labelled Edit chart data (appears only when the deck has a chart).
Open the Chart type select and choose Line, then Pie, then Bar.
Look at whether the chart preview changes to the chosen type, and compare with Expected.
S29.18.where: Artifact panel for a slide deck with a chart > Edit chart data > Chart type

S29.19.needs: a request to the assistant for a slide deck with a chart
S29.19.note: The editor shows a table of data rows, not a cell range such as B2:B5; the spreadsheet workbook charts have no range editor.
steps: Open a slide deck that contains a chart, as in S29.18.
Click Edit chart data.
Read the table of rows and columns (the first column is the label column, then one column per series).
Change a value, add or remove a row, and click the apply control; then compare the chart with Expected.
S29.19.where: Artifact panel for a slide deck with a chart > Edit chart data

S29.27.needs: a model and plan that allow code execution; a data file to upload is useful
S29.27.note: There is no separate Python analysis panel. Output appears as an expandable Code execution block (stdout, stderr, images); the code itself is not shown there as far as the code reveals. The Python Sandbox text in packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/v3.json is a card label, not a panel.
steps: Open a chat with a model that supports code execution.
Click the + button labelled Add attachment next to the chat box.
Turn on the Run code item (it is greyed out when the model or plan does not allow it).
Send a request that analyses data, then look for the Code execution block under the reply, expand it, and compare its stdout, stderr and images with Expected.
S29.27.where: Add attachment (+ button in the chat box) > Run code

S29.28.needs: a request to the assistant that returns a spreadsheet artifact
S29.28.note: The sortable table is the spreadsheet artifact (SpreadsheetArtifact.tsx, aria-sort on column headers). The markdown table has no sorting. The headings have no visible sort words.
steps: Ask the assistant for a table or spreadsheet of results, and wait for it to open in the artifact panel.
Click a column heading once to sort ascending, again to sort descending, and a third time to clear the sort.
Watch the rows reorder and the heading's sort state change.
Compare with Expected.
S29.28.where: Artifact panel for a spreadsheet > click a column heading

S29.34.needs: a request to the assistant that produces an .xlsx file
S29.34.note: The menu item appears only when the artifact has a generated file manifest; the original evidence line moved in the code. No button builds an .xlsx from a sheet on demand.
steps: Ask the assistant for a spreadsheet (.xlsx) and wait for it to appear in the artifact panel.
Click the Download button (title Download) in the artifact header.
Click Download generated file in the menu, if it is listed.
Open the downloaded file in a spreadsheet app and compare with Expected.
S29.34.where: Artifact panel for a spreadsheet > Download (button) > Download generated file

S29.35.needs: a request to the assistant for a table or spreadsheet
steps: Open a spreadsheet, table or CSV artifact in the artifact panel.
Click the Download button (title Download) in the artifact header.
Click Download as CSV.
Open the file that downloads, and compare its rows and columns with the artifact.
S29.35.where: Artifact panel for a spreadsheet > Download (button) > Download as CSV

S29.36.needs: a request to the assistant for a chart
S29.36.note: Chart export is PNG only, with an accessible name Download <chart name> as PNG; no SVG or CSV export for charts was found.
steps: Ask the assistant for a chart, and wait for it to draw in the chat.
Click the button with the Download icon and the text PNG in the chart's header.
Open the downloaded PNG file.
Compare the picture with the chart on screen.
S29.36.where: Chart artifact in the chat > PNG (button in the chart header)

S29.38.needs: a request to the assistant for a report
S29.38.note: No control turns an analysis into a report. Word and PDF are offered as downloads of a document artifact only. The line 'Writing report' is a progress label for research, not an export.
steps: Ask the assistant for a written report based on an analysis, and wait for the document artifact to open.
Click the Download button (title Download) in the artifact header.
Click Download as Word (.docx), then open the file; repeat with Download as PDF.
Compare the formatted file with the artifact text and with Expected.
S29.38.where: Artifact panel for a document > Download (button) > Download as Word (.docx)

S29.39.needs: a request to the assistant for a slide deck
S29.39.note: No pptx download item was found in the menus. Decks export only as PDF; a .pptx arrives only as a generated file through Download generated file, if the assistant made one. PptxFilePreview.tsx shows pptx files but does not download them.
steps: Ask the assistant for a slide deck based on an analysis, and wait for the deck to open in the artifact panel.
Click the Download button (title Download) in the artifact header.
Click Download as PDF and open the file.
Compare with Expected, which asks for a .pptx slide deck.
S29.39.where: Artifact panel for a slide deck > Download (button) > Download as PDF
